q: What will Yahweh do with the nations and most distant regions of the earth?
a: Yahweh will give them as an inheritance and possession.

q: From whom does salvation come?
a: Salvation comes from Yahweh.

q: What kind of sacrifices does David say to offer?
a: He says to offer sacrifices of righteousness.

q: What is David asking Yahweh to do because David is frail?
a: David asks Yahweh to have mercy on him and to heal him.

q: For what will David give thanks to Yahweh?
a: David will give thanks to Yahweh for his righteousness.

q: What does Yahweh think of righteousness?
a: He loves righteousness.

q: What does David ask that his heart might do?
a: He asks that his heart might rejoice in Yahweh’s salvation.

q: What does David want to come from Zion?
a: David wants the salvation of Israel to come from Zion.

q: From whom is David asking Yahweh to rescue him by his hand?
a: He is asking Yahweh to rescue him from men of this world whose prosperity is in this life alone.

q: Why did Yahweh save David?
a: Yahweh saved David because Yahweh delighted in him.

q: To whom does Yahweh show his covenant faithfulness?
a: He shows his covenant faithfulness to his anointed one, to David and to his descendants forever.

q: In what does the king rejoice?
a: He rejoices in Yahweh’s strength and in the salvation Yahweh provides.

q: Why is the king’s glory great?
a: His glory is great because of Yahweh’s salvation.

q: From what does David want to be rescued and saved?
a: He wants his life delivered from the sword, rescued from the hand of the dog, and saved from the mouth of the lion and the horns of wild oxen.

q: What does Yahweh anoint?
a: Yahweh anoints David’s head with oil.

q: Why should David not fear anyone?
a: David should not fear anyone since Yahweh is his light, his salvation, and the refuge of his life.

q: What are the faithful told to do in remembrance of Yahweh’s holiness?
a: The faithful are told to sing praise to Yahweh and to give him thanks.

q: With what does Yahweh surround the psalmist?
a: Yahweh surrounds him with shouts of deliverance.

q: What does Yahweh love?
a: Yahweh loves righteousness and justice.

q: In what will David rejoice?
a: He will rejoice in Yahweh’s salvation.

q: What is Yahweh’s righteousness like?
a: His righteousness is as permanent as the mountains of God, and his judgments are vast and mysterious as the deepest oceans.

q: Why does the psalmist say his whole body is sick?
a: His whole body is sick because of Yahweh’s anger, and there is no peace in his bones because of his sin.

q: What has David proclaimed in the great assembly?
a: He has proclaimed good news of God’s righteousness in the great assembly.

q: What has David not concealed?
a: He has not concealed God’s righteousness in his heart nor God’s covenant faithfulness nor trustworthiness from the great assembly.

q: What will Yahweh do for the blessed person on the bed of suffering?
a: Yahweh will support him on the bed of suffering and make his bed of sickness into a bed of healing.

q: What does the psalmist tell his soul to do?
a: He tells his soul to wait for God, for he will again thank God, the one who brings him salvation.

q: What does the psalmist ask God’s light and faithfulness to do?
a: He asks them to lead him and bring him to the mountain of God’s holiness and to God’s dwellings.

q: What does the psalmist tell his soul to do instead of being cast down?
a: He tells his soul to wait for God, for he will again thank God who is his salvation and his God.

q: How does the psalmist describe the king?
a: The king is fairer than the sons of man, grace is poured onto his lips, and God has blessed him forever.

q: Why should the king ride out?
a: The king should ride out for the sake of truth, humility, and righteousness.

q: What has the king loved and hated?
a: He loves righteousness and hates wickedness.

q: How does the psalmist describe God’s right hand?
a: His right hand is full of righteousness.

q: To whom will God show his salvation?
a: God will show his salvation to whoever offers a thank offering and orders their path rightly.

q: What does David ask God not to do to him?
a: He asks God to not cast him away from his presence, and to not take the Spirit of his holiness from him.

q: What does David ask God to restore to him?
a: He asks God to restore to him the joy of his salvation and to support him with a willing spirit.

q: What do David’s enemies do with their tongues?
a: They speak hostile things and cruel words which are like sharp swords.

q: What does the psalmist say about the person God chooses and brings near to dwell in his courts?
a: That person is happy and will be satisfied with the goodness of God’s house and the holiness of his temple.

q: Why should God be gracious to his people and bless them?
a: He should be gracious and bless them so that his way may be known on the earth and his salvation among all the nations.

q: What does God do for the lonely and the prisoners?
a: God provides families and homes for lonely people, and he brings prisoners out into prosperity.

q: What does David ask Yahweh to add to his enemies?
a: He asks Yahweh to punish them for all their sins and to not let them enter into Yahweh’s righteousness.

q: What will the psalmist proclaim with his mouth about Yahweh?
a: He will tell of Yahweh’s righteousness and salvation all day.

q: What does the psalmist say about God’s righteousness?
a: The psalmist says that God’s righteousness reaches to the heights and that no one is like God.

q: What does the psalmist do all day long?
a: He meditates on God’s righteousness all day long.

q: Why did Asaph’s feet nearly slip?
a: He nearly slipped because he was envious of the arrogant when he saw the prosperity of the wicked.

q: Why has God been Asaph’s king since ancient times?
a: Asaph recognizes God’s work of salvation in the earth and his power to create order out of chaos.

q: Why was Yahweh angry with Israel?
a: Yahweh was angry because they did not believe in him and did not trust in his salvation.

q: What will happen if Yahweh, the God of armies, restores the people?
a: If Yahweh restores them, they will be saved.

q: How does the psalmist ask God to treat the anointed king?
a: He asks God to treat favorably the king he has appointed to protect his people.

q: What will Yahweh do as he considers what to do?
a: Righteousness walks before Yahweh so he will recognize what the right thing is to do and he will do that.

q: How long has the psalmist been sick and on the verge of death?
a: Since he was young, the psalmist has been so ill that he has nearly died.

q: What did Yahweh say he will do for his chosen king David?
a: He said he had anointed him, will support him, strengthen him, and defeat his enemies.

q: What does the psalmist now say about how the anointed one is being treated by Yahweh?
a: The psalmist says that it appears that Yahweh has rejected the anointed king and has abandoned him.

q: What else does the psalmist ask the Lord to remember?
a: He asks the Lord to remember the insulting things people are saying about his people and how Yahweh’s enemies have been mocking the actions of his anointed king.

q: How does the psalmist describe Yahweh’s decrees and holiness?
a: The psalmist says that Yahweh’s decrees are completely reliable and his temple is a holy place.

q: What does the psalmist encourage everyone to announce?
a: The psalmist encourages everyone to announce that Yahweh has saved them.

q: What is the foundation of Yahweh’s throne?
a: The foundation of Yahweh’s throne is righteousness and justice.

q: What declares Yahweh’s righteousness and glory?
a: Everything that people can see in the heavens makes it clear that he is righteous and all the people groups see how glorious he is.

q: Why is Yahweh able to save his people?
a: Yahweh has saved his people by being powerfully holy.

q: Why did Yahweh save the psalmist’s ancestors?
a: He saved them because of who he is, so that he might show his power.

q: What do the people do on the day the king goes to battle?
a: They willingly offer themselves to serve him and show their devotion in holiness.

q: How long will Yahweh’s righteousness stand?
a: His righteousness will last forever.

q: In what ways did Yahweh rescue the psalmist?
a: Yahweh saved the psalmist from dying, from being sorrowful, and from making bad mistakes.

q: What does the psalmist ask Yahweh to allow him to do?
a: He asks Yahweh to allow him to truthfully tell others how Yahweh saved him.

q: What is the psalmist tired of waiting for?
a: He is tired of watching and waiting for Yahweh’s salvation which he has promised.

q: How long does every c of Yahweh’s righteousness last?
a: Every judgement Yahweh has made is right and will last forever.

q: What does David ask for concerning Jerusalem?
a: He asks that those living within the city walls will have peace and prosperity.

q: What did Yahweh do for the people of Israel?
a: Yahweh chose the descendants of Jacob, the people of Israel, to belong only to him as his special possession.

q: What did Yahweh do for David during battles?
a: Yahweh powerfully saved David and protected him during battles.

q: What does David ask Yahweh to do in response to his prayer?
a: David asks Yahweh to hear his prayer and answer him according to Yahweh’s faithfulness and righteousness.

q: What do people declare and sing about?
a: They will celebrate and declare Yahweh’s goodness and sing joyfully about his righteousness.
